skill.name: set-up-product-segmentation
skill.description: Set up and tune Product Segmentation in Product Metrics for Google Shopping and Performance Max: which Merchant Center custom label carries the segments and the category priority, the segmentation settings (date range, category column, excluded campaigns, margin or POAS, a target ROAS anchor, seasonality and competitor prices), product rules that set or lock a segment, and generating the supplemental feed. Use this skill when a merchant wants to segment products into custom labels, move the segments to another custom label, judge products on margin instead of revenue, keep a product line in Stars during a sale, or leave a campaign out of the segments. It previews every change and saves only the exact change the person confirmed. It works through Product Metrics, so use it even when Product Metrics is never mentioned. Not for connecting Merchant Center or Google Ads (connect-google-ads), reading the segments (check-product-segments), or building campaigns on them (check-campaign-structure).
skill.summary: Preview and approve Product Metrics segmentation settings, product rules, and Merchant Center label changes.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: All 55 static alerts are false positives: the backticks are Markdown, the URLs are documentation references, and the service operations are not system reconnaissance. Fixed draft names risk exposure or mix-ups, and the sale example assigns Stars without an expiry instead of locking existing segments. No evidence of prompt injection or data exfiltration was found in the skill.

remediation.issue: Settings drafts use fixed names with no storage or cleanup instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Use structured request bodies or a private, unique temporary directory. Reuse only the previewed draft for the approved property, and remove temporary files when finished.

remediation.issue: The winter sale example is named as a temporary lock but assigns Stars without an expiry.
remediation.suggestion: Use a keep action with an explicit end date for a temporary lock. Show the exact action and expiry in the preview and confirmation.

semantic_findings.title: Predictable local settings drafts
semantic_findings.description: The workflow writes settings snapshots to two fixed filenames without private storage or cleanup instructions. Shared workspaces can expose settings or mix drafts across runs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow names both files and reuses them for preview and update. Exposure or replacement depends on the workspace and its permissions.

content.user_title: Configure Product Segmentation for Google Shopping
content.value_statement: Changing segmentation settings can move products between groups used by Shopping and Performance Max campaigns. Preview the effect and approve the exact changes before they are saved in Product Metrics.
actual_capabilities: Check Merchant Center setup and read segmentation settings, custom label mappings, and product rules for the selected store.
Configure which Merchant Center labels carry the product segment and category priority.
Preview changes to date ranges, category sources, campaign exclusions, margin scoring, target ROAS, seasonality, and competitor price adjustments.
Preview which products a rule matches and which segments the rule would change.
Save approved settings or rules and read back the current state.
Request an immediate supplemental feed run instead of waiting for the nightly update.
limitations: Requires a configured Product Metrics CLI or MCP connection and an existing Merchant Center feed setup.
Saving requires write access and an editor or admin role. Feed generation requires a Product Segmentation subscription.
Previews estimate product moves. They do not guarantee campaign performance or confirm that Merchant Center has processed a new feed.
Does not connect accounts, build campaigns, or change campaign filters in Google Ads.

use_cases.title: Reserve custom labels for product segments
use_cases.description: Review existing label mappings and confirm which labels should carry product segments and category priority.

use_cases.title: Compare revenue and margin scoring
use_cases.description: Preview how profit-based scoring would move products between segments before changing the store's settings.

use_cases.title: Manage seasonal product exceptions
use_cases.description: Review which items match a proposed rule and confirm the action and expiry before holding their current segments during a sale.

prompt_templates.title: Review the current setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Check a store before proposing any edits.
prompt_templates.prompt: For [store name], check Merchant Center setup and tell me which custom labels carry the product segment and category priority. Do not make changes.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a new lookback period
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare a longer period with the current settings.
prompt_templates.prompt: For [store name], preview a 60-day segmentation lookback and keep the other settings unchanged. Show the expected product count and revenue by segment. Wait for my approval.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a seasonal rule
prompt_templates.scenario: Test a rule that preserves existing segments.
prompt_templates.prompt: For [store name], preview a rule that keeps the current segments for [product condition] until [end date]. Show the matched products, exact action, expiry, and expected moves. Do not create it yet.

prompt_templates.title: Test margin scoring with a campaign exclusion
prompt_templates.scenario: Review two interacting settings before an approved feed refresh.
prompt_templates.prompt: For [store name], preview margin-based scoring and exclude [campaign name] from segmentation calculations. Show the exact changes, predicted segment moves, and out-of-stock Stars. Ask me before saving and confirm separately before requesting an immediate feed run.

output_examples.input: Preview a 60-day lookback for the selected store without saving.
output: Illustrative preview: Change the lookback from 30 to 60 days. All other settings stay the same.
The draft puts 120 products and $18,400 in attributed revenue in Stars.
Nothing was saved. The change still needs your approval.

output_examples.input: I approve moving the product segment to Custom label 2 and keeping category priority on Custom label 1. Leave the feed on the nightly schedule.
output: Illustrative readback: Product segment is assigned to Custom label 2. Category priority remains on Custom label 1.
The supplemental feed is scheduled for the nightly run. No immediate run was requested.
Review any Shopping or Performance Max filters that still use the previous label.

best_practices: Confirm the store and feed before previewing changes.
Review existing label values, campaign filters, and each rule's action and expiry before approving a change.
Approve the exact changes after reviewing the preview, then verify the saved state and feed schedule.
anti_patterns: Overwrite an occupied label without checking its existing values and dependent campaign filters.
Treat a rule that assigns Stars as a temporary rule that preserves current segments.
Assume a saved change is already available in Merchant Center or reflected in campaign filters.

faq.question: Which advertising workflows does this support?
faq.answer: It configures Product Metrics segments used by Google Shopping and Performance Max through Merchant Center custom labels.

faq.question: Can I preview a change without saving it?
faq.answer: Yes. You can preview settings and rules, review the expected impact, and decline to save.

faq.question: Can I evaluate products on margin instead of revenue?
faq.answer: Yes. Preview profit-on-ad-spend scoring and review the predicted movement between segments before approving it.

faq.question: What happens if a custom label already has store values?
faq.answer: Product Metrics refuses the update unless an override is set. Approve an override only after reviewing which store values it would replace.

faq.question: What access do I need to save changes?
faq.answer: You need write access and an editor or admin role in Product Metrics. Generating a feed also requires a Product Segmentation subscription.

faq.question: When do saved changes reach the supplemental feed?
faq.answer: Saved settings and rules reach the feed on the nightly run. You can also approve an immediate run.
